newsitem.title: USA: NOPEC to supply soybean-based fuel to Iowa DOT.
newsitem.headline: NOPEC to supply soybean-based fuel to Iowa DOT.

text.p: NOPEC Corp, a privately-held company in Florida that makes environmentally friendly fuel, said Monday it has an order from the Iowa Department of Transportation.
The company declined to disclose the value of the agreement but said more than 23,000 gallons of its biodiesel fuel will be blended into the Iowa DOT's fuel in 1997.
The fuel to be used is soybean-based and will be mixed with Iowa DOT's supply of fuel to create a blend that is five percent biodiesel, NOPEC spokeswoman Karen Miller said.

NOPEC, which also makes other vegetable-based fuels, said its fuel requires no modifications to existing diesel engines and fuel facilities. The company's biodiesel fuel can be sold for as little $2.50 or $2.75 a gallon without shipping fees when it is is made from recycled cooking oil, Miller said.
The company also uses virgin vegetable oils to make biodiesel fuel.
NOPEC was founded about three years ago and the contract with the Iowa DOT is its first large order, Miller said.
Miller said the company's plant in Lakeland, Fla., can produce about 22 million gallons of biodiesel a year.
